questions.q: What should be the first question asked when diagnosing almost any Expenses issue?
options: What color is the expense report template?
Who is the CEO of the company?
At which of the six lifecycle stages does the reported symptom first appear?
What operating system is the employee using?
questions.explain: Locating which lifecycle stage (incur, capture, submit, audit/approve, account, reimburse) the symptom lives in determines what kind of fix is needed.

questions.q: In Ticket 1, why did Jordan Reyes's mileage claim calculate a lower amount than expected?
options: The updated $0.67/mile rate schedule had an effective date that started too late
He drove fewer miles than he claimed
His manager rejected the claim
Mileage claims require a receipt that he didn't attach
questions.explain: The new rate schedule's effective date was entered a week too late, so his claim processed under the old $0.65 rate instead.

questions.q: In Ticket 2, why did Priya's expense report sit in 'Pending Approval' for two weeks with no movement?
options: Priya never actually submitted the report
The report violated an audit rule and was permanently rejected
Her business unit had no expense templates configured
Her approver was on leave and no escalation rule was configured to forward the task automatically
questions.explain: The approval routed correctly to her supervisor, but with no escalation rule, the task simply sat unattended while he was on leave.

questions.q: In Ticket 3, why did the General Ledger's Travel & Lodging Expense balance not match what Payables showed as actually paid?
options: The General Ledger entries were posted incorrectly
Several Payables invoices failed import because of inactive employee supplier records, so the reimbursement payments never happened even though accounting had already posted
The employees never submitted any expense reports
Travel & Lodging Expense is not a real GL account
questions.explain: The accounting event (GL debit) had already posted correctly, but the resulting Payables invoices failed import due to inactive supplier records, creating the mismatch.

questions.q: What is the broader lesson all three tickets in this lesson illustrate?
options: The same surface symptom can originate from very different lifecycle stages, so diagnosis must start by locating the stage before attempting a fix
Every Expenses problem has the exact same root cause
Troubleshooting is impossible without calling Oracle support every time
Audit rules are unnecessary once approval rules exist
questions.explain: A 'stuck' or 'wrong' report can stem from capture, approval routing, or payment-stage issues — each needing a distinct fix, which is why locating the stage comes first.
